name: cpu_raytrace

libraries.name: Embree
libraries.usage: Builds the BVH over the scene triangles and performs all ray traversal (rtcIntersect1 for path segments, rtcOccluded1 for shadow rays); the path tracer on top of it is the measured workload.
libraries.notes: Built as a static library from the pinned submodule with the internal tasking system, triangle geometry only and runtime ISA dispatch; no source modifications. arm64 builds include Embree's vendored SSE2NEON header (MIT).

libraries.name: cgltf
libraries.usage: Parses the glTF models of the bundled scene before the measurement starts.
libraries.notes: Single header library compiled into the task from the pinned submodule; no source modifications.

libraries.name: nlohmann/json
libraries.usage: Parses the scene description (scene.json) before the measurement starts.
libraries.notes: Header only library compiled into the task from the pinned submodule; no source modifications.

libraries.name: stb
libraries.usage: Decodes the scene textures (JPEG) and the HDR environment map before the measurement, and encodes the rendered frame as PNG afterwards.
libraries.notes: Single header libraries compiled into the task from the pinned submodule; no source modifications.

libraries.name: Poly Haven scene assets
libraries.usage: The bundled models and HDR environment (common/assets/raytrace_scene/) that make up the rendered scene.
libraries.notes: Seven models and one HDRI, unmodified; the arrangement in scene.json is part of the task.

title: CPU ray traced rendering
short_description: Path traced render of a bundled scene on the processor.

structured_text.description: Renders a bundled 3D scene with a path tracer that runs entirely on the processor, tracing rays through a bounding volume hierarchy across all cores. The scene, sample count and resolution are fixed so the result depends only on the CPU.
structured_text.metric_explanation: The score is the number of completed render tiles per minute, reported as items per minute, which scales with how fast the full image is produced.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. More tiles per minute means shorter waits for a finished frame and faster iteration on lighting and materials.
structured_text.reasoning: CPU path tracing is still the backbone of high quality offline rendering, and it stresses floating point math, memory access and scheduling together, which makes it a strong stand in for 3D production.
